LESSON: LISTENING COMPREHENSION: LISTENING FOR DETAILS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Listening Comprehension: Listening for Details
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening Comprehension: Listening for Details, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What factors interfere with one’s ability to listen well? 2. How can you tell that people are listening attentively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify clues that signal details from a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening Comprehension: Listening for Details in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. take detailed notes on a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening Comprehension: Listening for Details in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of listening for details.  Search online or offline for signposts that introduce details in an oral text. Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using digital devices.  Listen and identify words that introduce different types of details that indicate: - addition such as first, also, moreover; - Emphasis such as an important note, especially, particularly; - Comparison such as. Like, similarly, just as - Contrast such as but, however, on the other hand; - Illustration such as for example, for instance, such as, - cause-and-effect such as because, therefore, so that, 1. What factors interfere with one’s ability to listen well? 2. How can you tell that people are listening attentively? 62  Discuss the kinds of details one should look out for from a text. The details could include numbers, figures, points, facts, examples, people, places, behaviour, and opinions, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Listen and note the clues signalling details from a peer,  Listen to a live or recorded oral presentation on a pertinent and contemporary issue such as natural resources, for example, forests, and take specific details,  Role-play, in turns, and make oral presentations as the partner takes notes. 63 Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they perform the activity. Assign activities according to each learner’s abilities.  Collaborate with peers to compare the notes, then revise and display for review.

1. Read this lesson on Listening Comprehension: Listening for Details together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Self-efficacy is developed as the learner listens for detail, thus making them confident in note-taking.

 Communication and collaboration are enhanced as the learner role-plays and makes oral presentations on pertinent and

contemporary issues forests as natural resources.

Values:
Patriotism is enhanced as the learners listens to texts on conservation of natural resources.

(PCIs)

Environmental and social issues are emphasised as the learner listens to texts on natural resources.

Link to other subjects:
